Cadillac Kicks Off 125th Anniversary With $239,000 Serialized Escalade-V Special Edition
29 photos
Photo: Cadillac / edited
Revealed ahead of the 2026 United States Grand Prix in Austin, Texas, the Escalade-V 125th Anniversary Collector Series is a very special brute. Capped at 252 units, every single example of this fellow is offered with pickable serial and vehicle identification numbers. Quite a cool personalization layer, and better still, it's stacked onto a performance SUV that is already exceptional in many regards.
Vehicles are to be labeled 1902 - 2027, and the production run will be split across two paint options. Cadillac bills the Escalade-V 125th Anniversary Collector Series as the opening act of its 125th anniversary celebrations, and furthermore, this model also marks the first Escalade to join the Collector Series .
As noted earlier, two finishes carry this program: Vibrant White Tricoat and Midnight Stone Frost. Both are exclusive to the special edition, with each taking 126 units, namely one per year from 1902 through 2027. A collector who chases a specific hue competes inside a pool of one, and the anniversary moolah buys a lot more than said experience. Visible carbon fiber is on the menu, featured on the mirror caps, engine cover, grille surround, and the lower rear fascia.
Forged 24-inch wheels add to the visual drama, framing blue-painted brake calipers. Dark-finish badging and heritage V8 puddle lamps make the 125th anniversary edition all that more desirable. Hopping inside, Cadillac went for a Black and Sheer Gray setup with eye-popping Santorini Blue stitching.
Photo: Cadillac Taking inspiration from the blue shade of the Mondrian pattern within the V-Series emblem, Santorini Blue is also used for the seat belts. A different shade of blue is used for the exclusive key fob, whereas the premium floor mats are said to have been created specifically for the Collector Series. Oddly for a V-Series model, the announcement for this one carries no maximum output figures.
Cadillac's media release does not touch on the supercharged V8 small block at all, though we do know the LT4 makes 682 horsepower and 653 pound-feet (885 Newton-meters) at full chatter in the Escalade-V. It's even punchier in the CT5-V Blackwing F1 Collector Series , in which the 6.2-liter unit develops 685 hp and 673 lb-ft (912 Nm) with the right fuel in optimal conditions.
Being an Escalade-V, the 125th Anniversary Collector Series isn't four-wheel drive. Instead, the Cadillac division of General Motors decided on all-wheel drive for this application. The full-time AWD system is the better pick than electronic 4WD for such a powerful road-oriented SUV because its active single-speed transfer case is tuned specifically for pavement-only performance, which also includes maximum launch traction.
Photo: Cadillac By comparison, the two-speed transfer case with low-range gearing is the better pick for towing and off-roading shenanigans. The Escalade-V further rocks an electronic rear limited-slip differential, actively shifting torque between the rear wheels to maximize cornering grip. The AWD system defaults to a fixed 50:50 split under normal conditions, yet the electronic brain can shift up to 67 percent to the rear wheels when pushing the vehicle hard.
Unique illuminated sill plates also mark Cadillac's birthday, and part of the $239,000 retail price can be traced back to said plates. The advertised price includes destination but excludes tax, title, and dealer fees. Given how rare this V8-powered brawler is, dealer ADMs may be truly insane.
Ordering for the first Collector Series Escalade is now open in both the US and Canada, the only markets getting this model. Global Caddy vice prez Kristian Aquilina frames the Escalade-V 125th Anniversary Collector Series as a celebration of Cadillac's heritage and the marque's approach to performance luxury, honoring the past while pointing at whatever comes next.
